data.body_html:
Andalusia Day (28 February) is the perfect excuse to swap the office for the open sea. With spring just around the corner, Marbella offers mild temperatures, sparkling Mediterranean waters, and a festive atmosphere that's uniquely Andalusian. A boat rental in Marbella lets you celebrate this regional holiday in style – cruising past the Golden Mile, toasting with cava, and soaking up views of La Concha. Here's everything you need to plan your 2025 celebration.

Why Celebrate Andalusia Day on a Boat?

Andalusia Day marks the 1980 referendum that granted the region autonomy. It's a public holiday in all eight provinces, and Marbella comes alive with flags, flamenco, and street parties. But the best way to experience the holiday is from the water. You'll avoid the crowded beaches, enjoy your own private space, and get a unique perspective of the Costa del Sol. With average February temperatures of 18-21°C and 11 hours of daylight, it's ideal for a day on the waves.

Our Fleet for the 2025 Celebration

All our charters depart from Puerto Banús, the heart of Marbella's luxury marina. Here's a selection to match your group size and budget:

For larger groups, consider the Mangusta 80 (Grey) or the K80 – both 24m and 12 pax. For an intimate celebration, the Dubhe (8m, 5 pax) is perfect. Browse the full fleet to see all options.

What's Included in Every Charter

No hidden costs, no surprises. Every rental includes:

  • Licensed skipper (and crew on larger yachts)
  • Fuel for the entire charter
  • Water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, and cava
  • Light snacks (olives, chips, nuts)
  • Insurance and safety equipment
  • Spanish IVA (21%)

That means you can relax and enjoy the celebration without worrying about extras.

Suggested Itinerary for Andalusia Day

Depart Puerto Banús at 11:00 and head east towards Marbella Marina. Pass the iconic Río Verde and the Golden Mile, then anchor at Cala del Faro for a swim (if you're brave – the water is around 15°C). Continue to Cala Cortés for a picnic lunch with a view of La Concha mountain. On the return, cruise past the luxury villas of Sotogrande if you've opted for a longer charter. For a sunset sail, book an 8-hour charter and stay out until 19:00.

Local Traditions to Enjoy Ashore

Before or after your boat trip, join the locals in Marbella's old town. You'll find free 'desayuno andaluz' (bread with olive oil and tomato) in the Plaza de los Naranjos. The official flag-raising ceremony takes place at the Town Hall at 12:00. In the evening, many bars offer free tapas – a perfect way to extend the celebration.

How to Book Your Boat for Andalusia Day 2025

Holiday weekends sell out quickly, so book early. For the best value, choose a Tier A boat (Astondoa 40 or Azimut 39) at €749 for 2 hours or €2,299 for 8 hours – ideal for a half-day or full-day celebration. If you want a touch of luxury, the Mangusta 80 at €4,719 for 4 hours includes a free jet ski. For other boats, contact us via WhatsApp for a custom quote. All bookings include free cancellation up to 48 hours before departure.
